the following two questions: i) how to design and implement a P2P system based on a virtual coordinate system, and ii) what are the benefits of such a system design.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Leopard is a P2P system that achieves the best of both worlds: i.e., it inherits the scalability of unstructured P2P networks and at the same time, achieves a routing stretch comparable to that of structured systems.
our system is a locality-aware P2P system that is able to achieve the above three desirable properties, and thus is a promising alternative approach to the current P2P paradigm.
the Leopard approach is a promising paradigm shift for P2P systems, and the proposed techniques are effective, scalable and practical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Leopard is a locality-aware peer-to-peer system with no hot spot.
Leopard is a locality aware P2P system that can provide near-optimal performance in a wide range of situations.
, by incorporating a virtual coordinate system and a geo-aware routing algorithm, we can build a P2P system with no hot spot, and the performance of this system is independent of the network size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network proximity information, which is critical in many P2P systems, can be obtained without excessive measurement or explicit maintenance.
a locality aware P2P network can be achieved by incorporating a virtual coordinate system in a P2P system, and the resulting system is not only efficient but also scalable.
, by incorporating the virtual coordinate system into the P2P network, we can achieve a P2P system with no hot spot and near optimal load balancing without sacrificing the performance of the system.
